claim: Each KLB GH1-like domain has lost at least one catalytic glutamate
finding: D1 acid/base E165(GBA3)->N241; D2 nucleophile E373(GBA3)->A889. Method validated: LPH regions III and IV recover their annotated catalytic pairs 4/4
context: human sequences; alignment transfer; GBA3 and BglB references
confidence: High. Limitation: pairwise global alignment, though CA RMSD 1.04-1.23 A superposition confirms the mapping

claim: No sugar-sized pocket remains in either KLB domain
finding: Buried cavity at the catalytic midpoint: GBA3 68.1 A3, KLB D1 4.0 A3, KLB D2 25.1 A3 apo and 1.0 A3 with FGF21 bound. Modelled glucose clashes with 12/12 (D1) and 8/12 (D2) heavy atoms
context: X-ray structures, grid probe 1.4 A, 0.5 A grid
confidence: High for D1. Medium for D2: an open ~110 A3 groove exists but is displaced from the glycone subsite

citation: This analysis (283 UniProt vertebrate KLB orthologs)
claim: Loss of the GH1 site is fixed across vertebrates
finding: D1 acid/base = Asn in 283/283; D2 nucleophile = Ala in 267/283, Glu in 0/283
confidence: High. Limitation: many entries are automatic gene predictions

claim: KLB is a receptor, not an enzyme; FGF21 binds its glycosidase-like region
finding: Crystal structures of free and FGF21CT-bound sKLB; KLB acts as a 'zip code'-like primary receptor and FGFR as the catalytic subunit

stance: refutes the D1 assignment in the seed hypothesis
claim: Which KLB pocket binds the FGF C-terminal tail
finding: FGF19CT and FGF21CT bind the same sKLB site: a D-P motif to site 1 and an S-P-S motif to the pseudoglycoside hydrolase region (site 2). Our contact map places S204-P205-S206 in the D2/KL2 pocket, not D1
context: human sKLB with FGF19CT and FGF21CT

claim: Both KL1 and KL2 contribute to FGF binding
finding: Both the KL1 and KL2 domains of beta-Klotho participate in ligand interaction and the sites are shared by FGF19 and FGF21
confidence: Medium-high; domain-level resolution, not residue-level for the pocket

claim: Klotho-family fold cannot support glycosidase catalysis
finding: 'The structure of alpha-klotho is incompatible with its purported glycosidase activity'; shed alpha-Klotho is a non-enzymatic scaffold
confidence: High for alpha-Klotho; applies to KLB by fold and residue homology

citation: PMID:24434184 (Andrukhova et al. 2014, EMBO Mol Med)
claim: alpha-Klotho acts on TRPV5 through glucuronidase/sialidase activity
finding: alpha-Klotho neither co-localizes with TRPV5 nor is regulated by FGF23; FGF23, not alpha-Klotho, is the calcium-conserving signal
context: mouse kidney, Fgf23 and Klotho knockouts

finding: Mutations of putative sialidase activity sites in soluble and membrane Klotho abrogated TRPV5 regulation; a sialidase inhibitor blocked the extracellular effect
confidence: Low-medium for enzymology; indirect, no purified-enzyme kinetics, alpha-Klotho not KLB

claim: Klotho acts as a sialidase on the TRPV5 N-glycan
finding: Klotho stimulation of TRPV5 was independent of the TRPV5 N-glycosylation state and klotho modified transferrin differently from sialidase
confidence: Medium; argues the Klotho effect is not sialidase chemistry

claim: GO:0004553 on KLB has no experimental basis
finding: GO:0004553 is IEA from InterPro GO_REF:0000002 via IPR001360 (family level). KLB matches no GH1 active-site signature (IPR018120, PS00572) and no PS00653
confidence: High for provenance. Caveat: GBA3 is active yet also lacks PS00572

finding: Source of the TAS GO:0008422 annotation on alpha-Klotho; a sequence-similarity inference from the original cloning paper
confidence: Low as enzymological evidence; historical inference
